questions.q: Two trains of length 240 m and 210 m are running on parallel tracks in opposite directions at speeds of 66 km/h and 54 km/h respectively. In how much time will they completely cross each other?
questions.solution: Combined speed is 120 km/h=100/3 m/s. Time to cover the combined 450 m length is 450÷(100/3)=13.5 seconds.

questions.q: A committee of 5 members is to be formed from 6 men and 4 women. In how many ways can this be done if the committee must include at least 3 women?
questions.solution: Possible compositions are 3 women+2 men and 4 women+1 man. Count =C(4,3)C(6,2)+C(4,4)C(6,1)=66.

questions.q: A started a business investing Rs. 50,000. After 4 months, B joined him investing Rs. 60,000. After 8 months from the start (i.e., with 4 months left in the year), A increased his investment by Rs. 20,000. If the total profit at the end of the year is Rs. 1,45,000, what is B's share of the profit?
The marked price of an article is Rs. 2,500. A shopkeeper allows two successive discounts of 20% and 10%, and still makes a profit of 20% on the cost price. What is the cost price of the article?
questions.solution: Selling price =2500×0.8×0.9=₹1800. This is 120% of cost, giving cost ₹1500.

questions.q: The ratio of the present ages of X and Y is 4:5. Eight years ago, the ratio of their ages was 7:9. What will be the ratio of their ages after 8 years?
questions.solution: Use ages 4k and 5k. The earlier ratio gives (4k−8)/(5k−8)=7/9, so k=16. Future ages are 72 and 88, ratio 9:11.

questions.q: A boat covers a distance of 90 km downstream in 5 hours and covers the same distance upstream in 9 hours. What is the speed of the boat in still water?
questions.solution: Downstream speed is 18 and upstream 10 km/h. Still-water speed is their average, 14 km/h.

questions.q: The difference between the compound interest (compounded annually) and the simple interest on a certain sum for 2 years at 12% per annum is Rs. 432. What is the sum?
questions.solution: For two years, CI−SI=P(0.12)². Thus P=432/0.0144=₹30000.

questions.q: Pipe A can fill an empty tank in 12 hours and Pipe B can fill it in 18 hours. Pipe C, a drain pipe, can empty the full tank in 9 hours. If all three pipes are opened together when the tank is empty, in how many hours will the tank be completely filled?
questions.solution: Net filling rate =1/12+1/18−1/9=1/36 tank per hour. Filling takes 36 hours.

questions.q: What is Meena's present age? Statement I: The present ages of Meena and her daughter are in the ratio 7:2, and the difference between their ages is 30 years. Statement II: Five years hence, the sum of Meena's age and her daughter's age will be 64 years.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II together are necessary to answer the question
Statement II alone is sufficient, while Statement I alone is not sufficient
Both Statement I and Statement II together are not sufficient to answer the question
Statement I alone is sufficient, while Statement II alone is not sufficient
Either Statement I alone or Statement II alone is sufficient
questions.solution: I alone gives ages 7k and 2k, with 5k=30, so Meena is 42. II alone only gives an age sum and cannot separate the two ages.

questions.q: A shopkeeper sold an article for Rs. 4,800, thereby earning some profit. What was the profit percentage? Statement I: Had he sold the article for Rs. 4,600, his profit would have been 15%. Statement II: The cost price of the article was Rs. 500 less than its marked price of Rs. 4,500.
options: Either Statement I alone or Statement II alone is sufficient
Statement II alone is sufficient, while Statement I alone is not sufficient
Statement I alone is sufficient, while Statement II alone is not sufficient
Both Statement I and Statement II together are necessary to answer the question
Both Statement I and Statement II together are not sufficient to answer the question
questions.solution: I gives cost =4600/1.15=₹4000. II independently gives cost =4500−500=₹4000. Either statement determines the profit percentage.

questions.q: What is the area of a rectangular field? Statement I: The length of the field is 4/3 times its breadth. Statement II: The perimeter of the field is 210 metres, and the length is 15 metres more than the breadth.
options: Statement I alone is sufficient, while Statement II alone is not sufficient
Statement II alone is sufficient, while Statement I alone is not sufficient
Both Statement I and Statement II together are necessary to answer the question
Either Statement I alone or Statement II alone is sufficient
Both Statement I and Statement II together are not sufficient to answer the question
questions.solution: I only fixes a ratio. II supplies sum of sides 105 and difference 15, giving length 60 and breadth 45, hence area 2700.

questions.q: Is the three-digit number N divisible by 6? Statement I: The sum of the digits of N is 18. Statement II: N is divisible by 4.
options: Statement I alone is sufficient, while Statement II alone is not sufficient
Both Statement I and Statement II together are necessary to answer the question
Statement II alone is sufficient, while Statement I alone is not sufficient
Either Statement I alone or Statement II alone is sufficient
Both Statement I and Statement II together are not sufficient to answer the question
questions.solution: I guarantees divisibility by 3 but not parity. II guarantees parity but not divisibility by 3. Together they guarantee divisibility by 6.

questions.q: A vessel contains a mixture of milk and water in the ratio 3:2. What is the quantity of water in the mixture? Statement I: The quantity of milk in the mixture is more than 24 litres. Statement II: The quantity of milk in the mixture is less than 36 litres.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II together are not sufficient to answer the question
Both Statement I and Statement II together are necessary to answer the question
Statement II alone is sufficient, while Statement I alone is not sufficient
Statement I alone is sufficient, while Statement II alone is not sufficient
Either Statement I alone or Statement II alone is sufficient
questions.solution: Together the milk amount can be any value between 24 and 36 litres. Water still has multiple possible amounts, so the data are insufficient.

questions.q: A cylindrical tank of radius 7 m and height 10 m is completely filled with water. This water is then emptied into a cuboidal tank of length 22 m and breadth 5 m. What will be the height of the water level in the cuboidal tank? (Use π = 22/7)
questions.solution: Cylinder volume =(22/7)×7²×10=1540 m³. Cuboid base area =22×5=110 m², so water height =1540/110=14 m.

questions.q: A vessel contains a mixture of milk and water in the ratio 5:3. If 24 litres of this mixture is removed and replaced with pure water, the ratio of milk to water becomes 5:7. What was the initial quantity of the mixture in the vessel?
questions.solution: Let initial volume be V. Milk after replacement is (5/8)(V−24), while final milk fraction is 5/12. Thus (5/8)(V−24)=5V/12, giving V=72 litres.
